name: The Emory
positioning: Modern hotel of suites and studios in Belgravia, London, designed by architect Richard Rogers, with views over Hyde Park
best_for: Travelers who want a private, residential-style suite with butler service
Wellness-focused guests who want access to the Surrenne Belgravia club
Families or groups who want to take a whole floor

facts.text: The Emory is in Belgravia, London.
Many suites have views over Hyde Park.
Works by Damien Hirst are displayed throughout the property.
The Surrenne spa spans four marbled subterranean floors.
The spa has a pool designed by Remi Tessier and a hyperbaric chamber.
Fitness guru Tracy Anderson has a studio in the Surrenne spa.
The City Circadian Reset is a personalised programme crafted to correct the circadian rhythm.
Each floor can be made interconnecting, allowing families up to eight interlinking suites.
abc kitchens brings chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten's abc brand to the UK for the first time.
The Emory Rooftop Bar serves cocktails overlooking the London skyline.
Knightsbridge is a quick hop to the west and Buckingham Palace a stroll to the east.

highlights.text: Guests can take exclusive use of an entire Private Floor, each floor individually crafted by a celebrated designer.
Every stay includes complimentary access to the Surrenne Belgravia wellbeing club.
The Emory is one of the last projects of architect Richard Rogers.
Suite and studio interiors are by designers Andre Fu, Pierre Yves Rochon, Alexandra Champalimaud, Rigby & Rigby and Patricia Urquiola.
Every stay includes an Emory Butler offering 24-hour personalised service.

considerations.text: The entrance is on the Old Barrack Yard side street and is barely marked.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
